sense: a diagram of figures or facts

terms.gloss: a chart or table (in a book or report)
evidence: M-O s.v. parts: table (in book), chart (Trappen 1843)
terms.comment: Classically a board, a writing tablet, a painting, a map (tabula picta), a list or account; the chart or table of a book is a modern use of it.

evidence: Vitr. 8.2, of maps of the world (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: A drawing out: Cicero’s word for the figures of the geometers. Far more often it means a description in words, or an arrangement (Lewis & Short).

evidence: M-O s.v. parts: table (in book), chart (Trappen 1843)
terms.comment: Classically a view or survey (see survey, an overview); a synopsis in Gellius.

phrases.latin: ratiōnem illī sententiae suae nōn ferē reddēbant, nisi quid erat numerīs aut dēscrīptiōnibus explicandum
phrases.english: they hardly ever gave reasons for their views, unless something had to be explained with numbers or diagrams

sources: Lewis & Short: tabula · Lewis & Short: descriptio · Lewis & Short: conspectus
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. parts: table (in book), chart.
